title: Johnny Dunn and the French horn mix-up
summary: Holmes remembers Johnny Dunn as a publicity-heavy trumpeter whose reign was over by 1927, and admits he is unobservant about how brass instruments are built.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: What about some other trumpeters that you remember, going all the way back to, say, Johnny Dunn?
Well, Johnny Dunn was about... He was a sensation. He's the one had the publicity, the big note and the long horn, the long coach horn. And he was the king of the valves.
Did the coach horn have valves or not?
Yeah, I think so..
It had valves.
I think so. I don't know. I wasn't
Holmes (1/14) - 34

interested in how they were built. In fact, do you know something? I just found out a few years ago, and I played in a symphony band, I started out in a symphony orchestra... And I just found out a few years ago that a French horn was fingered with the left hand.
Uh-huh.
You understand what I mean?
Yeah.

A French horn. I just found that out a few years ago. I thought it was fingered with the right hand all the time. So I'm not observant on how instruments are built, unless I'm playing it. The brass instruments, I don't notice them at all. That was funny... It tickles me how stupid I was about the French horn. I was so surprised when I found out that was a left-handed horn. But now, what was I talking about?
We were on Johnny Dunn.
Oh, Johnny Dunn, yeah. Yeah. I don't know if the coach horn had valves or not. I imagine they did. I'm not sure. But that's what he used to play!
Did he sort of have an act? Or was he leading a band?
I don't know. I'd never see him perform. I wouldn't spend no money to hear him. He wasn't that good to me, and I never heard him (you know what I mean?)
Holmes (1/14) - 35
perform. I heard him play...
But he was a big name when you came to New York.

He was a big name. Yeah, he was the big man. But see, no, when I come here, I guess he was kind of out of business. Because see, Louis had been here with Fletcher in '25. I came in '27. So I didn't hear much of Johnny Dunn.
No, he was gone by then.
Yes. He wasn't the King no more.
